newsitem.title: UK: ICCO-led cocoa committee in Abidjan for reform talks.
newsitem.headline: ICCO-led cocoa committee in Abidjan for reform talks.

text.p: A consultative committee led by the International Cocoa Organization (ICCO) started a three-day meeting in Abidjan on Wednesday, in the first of planned missions to review the cocoa reform process currently underway in West Africa.

The ICCO said in a statement that the aim of the committee, consisting of 10 people including the spokesmen for ICCO consumer and producer countries and industry experts, was to consider solutions to problems that have arisen after the liberalisation of the marketing of cocoa.
"It is vital to address the problems encountered with the introduction of the liberalisation process," said Edouard Kouame, ICCO executive director who heads the mission.

The committee will meet every six months to monitor the operation of the world cocoa market following the reform and serve to exchange information between Ivorian authorities and lending organisations such as the World Bank and the IMF.

Cocoa experts have suggested that corrective measures were urgently needed in Cameroon and Nigeria, and accompanying measures introduced in Ivory Coast to allow full and effective participation of the local operators to the marketing systems.

The committee was established after a series of missions to Washington and West Africa to highlight concerns of the cocoa community regarding liberalisation. The ICCO will further discuss the issue at its Council session in March to draft a full project for possible funding by the Common Fund for Commodities.
